topics.title: Functions of Several Variables
topics.explanation:
A function of several variables takes more than one input. For example, z = f(x, y) maps two independent variables to one output.

Visual analogy: (x, y) is your position on the ground and z is the height of the terrain. The graph is a surface in 3D space.

Example: f(x, y) = x² + y² is a paraboloid. At (0,0) the value is 0. At (1,2) the value is 5.

questions.question: Describe the surface z = x² + y². What is f(1, 2)?

topics.title: Limits & Continuity in Higher Dimensions
topics.explanation:
In multivariable calculus a limit exists only if the function approaches the same value along every possible path to the point.

Path test: Substitute y = mx. If the result depends on m, the limit does not exist.

Example: lim (x,y)→(0,0) of xy/(x²+y²). Along y = mx the limit is m/(1+m²), which changes with m. Hence the limit does not exist.

For piecewise continuity at a boundary, left-hand limit must equal right-hand limit must equal the function value.

questions.question: Show that lim (x,y)→(0,0) of xy/(x² + y²) does not exist.
questions.solution: Along y = mx, limit = m/(1+m²). Different m give different values. Limit does not exist.

questions.question: Find A so that f(x) = A + x for x < 2 and 1 + x² for x ≥ 2 is continuous at x = 2.
Find B so that f(x) = 2x² + 3 for x ≤ 2 and 3x + B for x > 2 is continuous at x = 2.

topics.title: Partial Derivatives & Clairaut’s Theorem
topics.explanation:
Partial derivative with respect to x treats y as constant. Partial with respect to y treats x as constant.

Example: f(x,y) = x² + y² + x²y² → fx = 2x + 2xy², fy = 2y + 2x²y.

Clairaut’s Theorem: If the second partials are continuous, then fxy = fyx.

questions.question: If f(x,y) = x² + y² + x²y², find all first-order partial derivatives.
Find all first-order partials of f(x,y) = 6x² + 13xy + 4y².

topics.title: Chain Rule & Total Differentials
topics.explanation:
If z = f(x,y) and x = x(t), y = y(t), then dz/dt = fx dx/dt + fy dy/dt.

For total differential coefficient under a constraint, differentiate the constraint implicitly to find dy/dx, then substitute into the total derivative formula.

questions.question: Find the total differential coefficient of u = x²y with respect to x where x² + xy + y² = 1.

topics.title: Homogeneous Functions & Euler’s Theorem
topics.explanation:
A function is homogeneous of degree n if f(tx, ty) = tⁿ f(x,y).

Euler’s Theorem: x ux + y uy = n u.

This is a standard 5-mark proof question.

questions.question: State and prove Euler’s theorem on homogeneous functions.
questions.solution: Write u = xⁿ F(y/x). Differentiate partially and add after multiplying by x and y.

questions.question: Verify Euler’s theorem for u = x³ + 3x²y + 3xy² + y³.

topics.title: Gradient, Directional Derivatives & Extrema
topics.explanation:
Gradient of Φ(x,y,z) is ∇Φ = Φx i + Φy j + Φz k.

Directional derivative in direction of unit vector û is ∇Φ · û.

For extrema of f(x,y): solve fx = 0, fy = 0. Then compute Δ = fxx fyy - (fxy)². If Δ > 0 and fxx > 0, relative minimum. If Δ > 0 and fxx < 0, relative maximum. If Δ < 0, saddle point.

questions.question: Find ∇Φ for Φ = 3x²y - y³z² at (1, -2, -1).
Find the directional derivative of f = xyz at (1,-1,1) in the direction of 3i - 4k.
Classify the relative extrema of f(x,y) = 6x² + 10y² + 2x - 3y + 15.

topics.title: Convergence Tests
topics.explanation:
An infinite series converges if the sequence of partial sums approaches a finite limit.

Key tests: nth-term test, geometric series, p-series, ratio test, root test, Leibniz alternating test.

questions.question: Evaluate the sum from i=1 to 4 of (2n + 3).
Test the convergence of the series ∑ n / 2ⁿ using the ratio test.

topics.title: Taylor & Maclaurin Series
topics.explanation:
Maclaurin series is the Taylor series expanded about x = 0.

ex = 1 + x + x²/2! + x³/3! + ...

sin x = x - x³/3! + x⁵/5! - ...

ln(1+x) = x - x²/2 + x³/3 - ...

questions.question: Derive the Maclaurin series for eˣ.
questions.solution: All derivatives at 0 are 1. Series is ∑ xⁿ/n!.

topics.title: Improper Integrals
topics.explanation:
Type 1: infinite limits. Type 2: integrand becomes infinite inside the interval.

Example: ∫ from 1 to ∞ of 1/x² dx = 1 (convergent).

questions.question: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to ∞ of e⁻³ˣ dx.

topics.title: Beta & Gamma Functions
topics.explanation:
Γ(n) = ∫ from 0 to ∞ of xⁿ⁻¹ e⁻ˣ dx. Γ(n+1) = nΓ(n). Γ(1/2) = √π.

B(m,n) = ∫ from 0 to 1 of xᵐ⁻¹ (1-x)ⁿ⁻¹ dx. B(m,n) = Γ(m)Γ(n)/Γ(m+n).

questions.question: Prove that B(m,n) = B(n,m).
Find Γ(5/2).

topics.title: Area & Volume of Revolution
topics.explanation: Disk method and shell method are used for volumes of solids of revolution. Area between curves is found by definite integration.

questions.question: Find the volume generated by revolving y = x² from x = 1 to 3 about the y-axis.

topics.title: Double & Triple Integrals
topics.explanation: Double and triple integrals can be evaluated as iterated integrals. Order of integration can be changed when needed. Polar coordinates are useful for circular regions.

questions.question: Evaluate the triple integral of xy²z over the region 0≤x≤2, 1≤y≤3, 1≤z≤2.

topics.title: Divergence, Curl & Theorems
topics.explanation: Divergence measures outward flux. Curl measures rotation. Green’s, Stokes’, and Gauss’s theorems relate line, surface, and volume integrals (statements only required for most exams).

questions.question: State Gauss’s divergence theorem.

topics.title: First-Order Linear ODEs
topics.explanation: First-order linear equations are solved using an integrating factor. For dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x), the integrating factor is e^∫P dx.

questions.question: Solve dy/dx + 2xy = 4x.

topics.title: Cauchy-Euler & Legendre
topics.explanation: Cauchy-Euler equations use the substitution x = eᶻ. Legendre polynomials satisfy a specific second-order ODE and have Rodrigues’ formula.

questions.question: Write Rodrigues’ formula for Legendre polynomials.
